documents.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
documents.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics an

documents.title: Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.
documents.abstract: The Hofmeister series is a fundamental paradigm for ion-specific regulation of protein properties, with anions playing a dominant role. However, its molecular mechanism remains long-debated, and a systematic synthesis linking basic theory to food protein processing practices is still lacking. This review dissects the action mechanisms of Hofmeister anions from water structure regulation and ion-protein interactions, and summarizes their applications in protein extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization and structural modification. The principal finding is that the Hofmeister effect arises fr

documents.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump.
documents.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å r

documents.title: From passive deposition to signal-guided targeting: a functional outer layer enables preferential stomatal colonization by a microbial herbicide.
documents.abstract: Foliar-applied microbial herbicides in the field face two interrelated bottlenecks: rapid viability loss caused by environmental stresses and passive stochastic deposition that restricts contact with host entry sites.

documents.title: Advances in photothermal nanozymes: from rational design to multifunctional theranostic platforms.
documents.abstract: Photothermal nanozymes integrate enzyme-like catalysis with photothermal conversion, where localized hyperthermia accelerates kinetics, improves substrate accessibility, and modulates biological barriers to achieve synergistic amplification beyond monotherapies. This review systematically surveys design strategies and applications, with highlights centered on three interconnected aspects. A composition-based classification framework is first established, covering noble metals, transition metal compounds, carbon-based materials, Prussian blue analogues, single-atom catalysts, and metal-organic

documents.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
documents.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall

documents.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.
documents.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to euk

documents.title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists.
documents.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. However, the structural complexity and conformational plasticity of class B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) make conventiona
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
documents.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular mode
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
documents.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactyla

documents.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
documents.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. Whether and when these challenges demand more sophisticated physical models has remained an open question. Here, we address it th
documents.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation

documents.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
documents.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. Conventional sequence

documents.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
documents.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. Here, we describe CovPDB v2.0, a substantially extended release that addresses three main limitations of the original resource. First, to reflect the numerous novel covalently binding ligands d

documents.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
documents.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap

documents.title: Conformational Plasticity of Orthosteric Pocket Enables the Discovery of a Novel PAD4-Selective Inhibitor.
documents.abstract: Peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PAD) family enzymes are pivotal enzymes that catalyze the citrullination of arginine in substrate proteins. Elevated levels of citrullinated proteins are tightly linked to the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancers, thus highlighting PAD enzymes as important therapeutic targets. Although several PAD isozyme-selective and non-selective small molecule inhibitors have been reported over the last decade, it remains important to identify distinct ligands that may offer differentiated therapeutic potential or selectivity. Herein, we pr

documents.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
documents.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short serv

documents.title: Minimal Mutagenesis Resurrects Human Uricase with Attenuated Immunogenicity.
documents.abstract: The human uricase (UOX) gene was pseudogenized during evolution, leaving uric acid as the terminal product of purine metabolism. Heterologous uricases can elicit anti-drug antibodies, which limit their long-term use. Here, we restored activity to a human-pseudogene-derived uricase reference through molecular-evolution-guided rational design. Sequence alignment guided the construction of reversion mutants by overlap-extension PCR and two rounds of combinatorial optimization. Structural modeling and an accelerated co-culture dendritic cell (acDC) assay were used to generate mechanistic hypothese

documents.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. documents.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
documents.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. documents.title: Inclusion-Based Micromechanics in Nanostructured Media.
documents.abstract: The Eshelby theory supports inclusion-based micromechanics and provides a common framework for connecting microstructural heterogeneities, eigenstrains and effective material properties. The conventional formulations assume ellipsoidal shapes, uniform internal strain fields, and perfectly bonded interfaces. At the nanoscale, these assumptions are limited by high surface-to-volume ratios, surface and interface elasticity, interfacial imperfections and irregular geometries, which may substantially affect local mechanical fields and overall material response. This review summarizes recent extensi

documents.title: Molecular Scale Modelling and Chemical and Mechanical Characterization of Graphene-Oxide-Reinforced Calcium Silicate Hydrate (C-S-H) Using Reactive Force Field (ReaxFF).
documents.abstract: Graphene and graphene oxide (GO) exhibit exceptional tensile strength and elastic modulus, and the functional groups on GO promote dispersion and accelerate hydration in cementitious matrices. This study uses molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the mechanical behaviour of graphene/GO-reinforced calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) at the nanoscale. A reactive force field (ReaxFF) with modified C/O parameters was developed to describe atomic interactions between C-S-H and graphene/GO. A more realistic C-S-H structure with varying calcium-to-silicon (Ca:Si) ratios was produced by remo

documents.title: Tannic Acid Inhibits CaMKII-β Kinase Activity In Vitro and Displays Preclinical Anti-Tumor Activity in Ovarian Cancer Models.
documents.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is characterized by delayed clinical diagnosis, intrinsic/acquired platinum chemoresistance, and a high postoperative recurrence rate, highlighting an unmet clinical need for new targeted therapeutic strategies. Herein, we integrated pan-cancer transcriptomic profiling, clinical tissue immunohistochemistry, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, co-immunoprecipitation, structure-based virtual ligand screening, in vitro kinase activity assays, cellular viability functional assays, and SK-OV-3 xenograft mouse models to preliminarily reveal that CaMKII-β may mediate OC progression and

documents.title: Cavity-Guided Chemiluminescent Probes for Drug-Metabolizing Enzymes: Rational Design , Activity Imaging, and Translational Applications.
documents.abstract: Drug-metabolizing enzymes (DMEs), which are crucial for xenobiotic biotransformation, profoundly influence therapeutic efficacy, drug safety, and physiological homeostasis. However, conventional analytical methods such as LC-MS/MS and fluorescence-based assays face limitations in background interference, spatiotemporal resolution, and in vivo imaging, while the structurally diverse catalytic cavities and overlapping substrate preferences of DMEs complicate isoform-specific activity assessment. In this context, chemiluminescence (CL) probes, particularly programmable Schaap-type 1,2-dioxetanes

documents.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space.
documents.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ∼3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: In Silico-Guided Screening of a High-Affinity PD-L1 Aptamer for the Construction of a Sensitive Electrochemical Aptasensor.
documents.abstract: Programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an essential immune checkpoint protein that plays a pivotal role in tumor immune evasion and has emerged as an important biomarker for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and immunotherapy monitoring. Aptamers have attracted increasing attention as promising molecular recognition elements owing to their high specificity, excellent chemical stability, and facile synthesis. In this study, we developed an in silico-guided aptamer screening strategy that integrates virtual library construction, molecular docking, secondary structure prediction, and structural interact

documents.title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer's Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes.
documents.abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators ( R1-R5 ). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. Comparative docking against Rab5, Rab8, and Rab11 predicted preferential interactions with GTP-associated Rab10. R

documents.title: Effects of Graphene Incorporation on the Nanoscale Structure and Mechanical Response of PVDF Membrane Models: A Molecular Dynamics Study.
documents.abstract: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) membranes require both suitable morphology and mechanical integrity, but changes in nanoscale geometry do not necessarily improve all loading responses. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations were used to compare pristine PVDF and graphene/PVDF membrane models constructed from five-repeat-unit oligomers. A force-driven sedimentation procedure was used to examine the effects of lateral cell size and polymer-chain number on deposited morphology. The structural indicator was a two-dimensional projected void-area fraction. Increasing polymer-chain number reduced

documents.title: A structure-derived contact-network responsiveness atlas of human proteins.
documents.abstract: Protein structures encode non-local contact organization, but static coordinates do not directly quantify how a contact network responds when effective stabilizing interactions are strengthened or weakened. Here we introduce Contact-Network Responsiveness (CNR), a structure-derived framework that converts residue-level protein coordinates into density-controlled and topology-corrected response descriptors. documents.title: Comparative Binding Profiles of Co-Crystallized Ligands at Human Phosphodiesterase 1B Using Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Binding Free Energy Analysis.
documents.abstract: Phosphodiesterases (PDEs) biochemically break down cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) and cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP), which functionally regulate cyclic nucleotide signaling pathways. cAMP/cGMP signaling has been associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease (AD). The present in silico study focuses on the three co-crystallized ligands 0NY, 8HM, and 8HP bound to phosphodiesterase 1B (PDE1B), assessing structural stability via root mean square deviation (RMSD), conformational dynamics via root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), and hydrogen bonding and binding

documents.title: Effects of Ultrasound on the Enzymatic Hydrolysis and Bioactivities of Food Protein Hydrolysates: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
documents.abstract: Enzymatic hydrolysis is widely used to produce food protein hydrolysates enriched in bioactive peptides, but its efficiency can be enhanced by auxiliary technologies such as ultrasound. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of ultrasound on the enzymatic hydrolysis of food-derived protein matrices, emphasizing the degree of hydrolysis and bioactivities of the resulting hydrolysates. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase identified 55 eligible studies published between 2013 and 2026, of which 35 were included in the meta-analysis. The include

documents.title: Diversity at the Acinetobacter baumannii K locus: towards a comprehensive database for in silico prediction of capsular polysaccharide types.
documents.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is one of the most critical bacterial pathogens requiring novel approaches for infection control and treatment to curb the spread of highly resistant isolates. Epidemiological surveillance and the design and application of many non-antibiotic interventions require rapid and accurate prediction of diverse capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types from whole-genome sequence data. The internationally adopted CPS typing system relies on the in silico detection of CPS biosynthesis genes both in and outside the K locus (KL), utilizing a reference sequence database that is compatibl

documents.title: Protective Effects of Spirulina on Obesity-Induced Renal Damage and Oxidative Imbalance: Computational and Experimental Study.
documents.abstract: Obesity, primarily driven by high-calorie and high-fat diets, is a major public health issue and a key risk factor for kidney dysfunction. It triggers glomerular hyperfiltration and oxidative stress, which can lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Spirulina has emerged as a potent natural agent with strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Membranes Aid in Understanding Resistance Mechanism to Polymyxin B1.
documents.abstract: One of the major causes for hospital acquired infections is multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains. Polymyxins are a group of lipopeptide antibiotics used as a last-line resort for treatment of Gram-negative infections. Polymyxins initially target Lipid A's of lipopolysaccharides in the bacterial outer membrane via both electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Resistance to polymyxins in P. aeruginosa includes modification of Lipid A's to attenuate the interactions with polymyxins but to date our understanding of underlying mechanisms is still limited. documents.title: Activity-Guided Discovery and Functional Characterization of VTPPHVE, a Tyrosinase-Inhibitory Peptide from Golden Pompano (Trachinotus anak) Muscle Proteins.
documents.abstract: Marine-derived bioactive peptides are promising natural enzyme inhibitors, but their functional robustness and inhibition behavior require experimental validation. Golden pompano (Trachinotus anak) muscle proteins were subjected to ultrasound-assisted neutral protease-papain hydrolysis, activity-guided ultrafiltration, LC-MS/MS identification, and synthetic-peptide validation. The <3 kDa ultrafiltration fraction showed the highest activity (75.43% tyrosinase inhibition and 51.40% apparent Cu2+ chelation) and was selected for LC-MS/MS. documents.title: Rational Design of Benzofuran-Linked Isatin Derivatives as MTDLs Targeting MAO-B and Cholinesterases: Synthesis, in silico Insights, and Neuroprotection Studies.
documents.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are multifactorial diseases associated with oxid active stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalance, leading to progressive neuronal loss. Since monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) contributes to dopamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species generation, it represents an attractive therapeutic target for anti-neurodegenerative drug discovery. This study aimed to develop novel benzofuran-isatin hybrids within a multitarget-directed ligand (MTDL) strategy to achieve selective MAO-B inhibition combined with cholinesterase inhibitory and neuroprotective a

documents.title: Aggregate-associated interfacial organization of sodium oleate near zircon surfaces.
documents.abstract: Sodium oleate (NaOL) is widely used as an anionic collector for zircon flotation, yet its heterogeneous organization at zircon surfaces remains insufficiently characterized.

documents.title: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics-Based Investigation of the Potential Anti-Inflammatory and Cell-Survival Regulatory Mechanisms of Dapansutrile in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
documents.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage and bone destruction, and disability. Existing therapies can be limited by adverse effects and cost, and additional treatment approaches remain of interest. Dapansutrile (OLT1177) is an orally active, selective inhibitor of the NLRP3 inflammasome that has shown anti-inflammatory activity and good tolerability in early clinical studies. Whether dapansutrile might also interact with other RA-related proteins has not been examined specifically in RA. This study used c
documents.journal: Open access rheumatology : research and reviews

documents.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
documents.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli,

documents.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
documents.abstract: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD).

documents.title: PARP1 and PD-L1 dual-targeted bifunctional small-molecule inhibitors: a novel strategy for dual immunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer.
documents.abstract: Current single-agent PD-L1 immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combination regimens have several drawbacks, including limited response rates, mismatched pharmacokinetics, and overlapping toxicities. This research aims to discover novel bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously block the PD-1/PD-L1 axis and PARP1, with prominent selectivity for PARP subtypes, to overcome bottlenecks in triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy.

documents.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
documents.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. documents.title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
documents.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. Methods: We analyzed the spatial distribution of key metabolites in GBM patients and orthotopic xenograft mouse

documents.title: Advances in injectable liposome-microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification.
documents.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. Injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) systems have recently emerged as integrative delivery platforms that synergistically combine t

documents.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
documents.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1.
